BLOCKER: AC "gate_decide refuses in CI" is unimplemented: `--hil-confirmed` is just a flag any caller (including CI) can pass; there is no CI/automation detection or attestation.
AC "validates accepted_risks {owner, until, rationale}" is absent from the diff — no schema check anywhere in gate_decisions.py or the approval path.

AC "SCOPE findings resolved only with a follow-up item / non-blocking" is unenforced: only `DISPOSITION_STATUSES` gains "SCOPE"; no check that a SCOPE finding references a follow-up item, and no approval-path handling.
Required tests missing: gate0 negative/positive, SCOPE resolution, accepted-risk validation, duplicate-review refusal — only `test_gate_decisions.py` is added.
AC "gate-brief renders the reconciliation and impact-review table for HIL" is unimplemented; only `gate0_check.render` exists (no gate-brief wiring in the diff).
MAJOR: `gate0_check.transitions()` fails open: unreadable/missing item JSON is `continue`d, and `git show` failure yields `prev={}`, so a transition can silently escape the gate.
Gate 0 API/AC row detection is substring-based (`"api" in claims`), so any claim containing "api" (e.g. "capital") satisfies the API row; same weak match for "ac"/"language".
COMPLIANCE one-way-door validation is duplicated in `retentionFor` (Put) and `ApplyLifecycle`, plus a third variant in LocalStore.Put — the irreversible policy will drift between paths.
`LocalStore.keyLocks` grows unbounded per key (long-lived process leak), and `Delete`/`DeleteVersion` never take the key lock, so `Immutable` can be raced by a concurrent delete/re-put.
`go_modules_check._git_changed()` catches all exceptions and returns `[]`, interpreted as "no Go changes" → the entire module gate is skipped on any git failure (fail-open in CI).

`precheck.py` hardcodes a "parallel_safe" allowlist asserting several gates (wired-audit, intent-trace, docs-fresh, api-contract) are read-only without verification, and the fast tier no longer runs the full suite — coverage regression hidden behind speed.
MINOR: Decision record hardcodes `"hil_confirmed": True` instead of recording the actual flag value; no evidence beyond the flag that a human approved.
`objpolicy.Stats()` is process-local and lost on restart; per-tenant denial counts are not exported to metrics, weakening the "counted per tenant+reason" observability claim.
Tenant scoping in `Mint` is a pure string-prefix check with a hardcoded `<tenant>/` naming convention and no registry; enforcement depends entirely on adapter key hygiene.
Gate 0 only inspects current status `in_progress` vs previous not-in_progress; re-grooming edits to an already-in_progress item (or regressions from completed) are never re-checked.
Duplicate-review refusal is TOCTOU (file-existence check with no lock) and keyed only by filename; concurrent reviews of the same sha both proceed.
NIT: `S3Store.Capabilities` acquires and releases `lockMu` twice back-to-back; one critical section suffices.
`gate0_check.problems` treats whitespace-only reconciliation values as present (truthy).
Trailing newline-only change at end of `go_modules_check.py` adds diff noise.
SUMMARY: The Go work (EDP-16 lifecycle, objpolicy boundary, read-only reconcile) is directionally sound and mostly fail-closed, but this diff does not deliver most of BI-PF-1471's acceptance criteria: CI refusal, accepted-risk validation, SCOPE follow-up enforcement, gate-brief rendering, and 4 of 5 required test areas are missing.
The new Python gates additionally fail open on git/IO errors and rely on substring heuristics, so Gate 0 can be bypassed by a malformed item or a lucky claim wording.
Top risks: an unenforceable human-only gate (a flag, not an attestation), immutable-object bypass via unlocked deletes, and CI checks that silently self-disable on tooling errors.
